title: When & While
description: Connect a continuing background action with a shorter past event.
objectives: Connect a continuing background action with a shorter past event.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to connect a continuing background action with a shorter past event. The central language is past continuous with while and past simple with when. It belongs to the practical context of stories & experiences. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: past continuous with while and past simple with when

blocks.english: While I was cooking, the phone rang.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the when & while exchange.

blocks.english: I met Ava when I was traveling.
blocks.explanation: This when & while model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the when & while exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “While I was cooking, the phone rang.” and “I met Ava when I was traveling.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: past continuous with while and past simple with when.
